title: Bangladeshi Man Pleads Guilty in Human Smuggling Case Tied to Laredo Crossings
excerpt: Sajib Kumar Saha, 32, of Bangladesh pleaded guilty to conspiring to transport undocumented migrants for financial gain, in a case prosecutors say moved Bangladeshi migrants along a Panama–Colombia route and through the Laredo area.
content:
Sajib Kumar Saha, 32, of Bangladesh pleaded guilty to one count of conspiracy to transport undocumented noncitizens for financial gain, according to the Laredo Morning Times. He entered the plea before U.S. District Judge Marina Garcia Marmolejo.

Sentencing is set for Feb. 17, according to the report. The charge carries a mandatory minimum of three years in prison, and Saha agreed to forfeit at least $12,000.

Prosecutors said Saha was an organizer who arranged travel for Bangladeshi migrants along a Panama–Colombia route, with each migrant paying $6,000, according to the report. Two Bangladeshi men crossed into the United States near Rio Bravo in February 2024, paid Saha, and he wired money to Brazil and planned to travel there to collect payment, according to the report.

Saha was arrested in Houston in December 2024, according to the report.

Homeland Security Investigations said more than 7,000 Bangladeshi nationals have been encountered near Laredo and in South Texas since October 2024, according to the report.

Source: Laredo Morning Times, Nov. 15, 2026.
